  -- FAIL (4) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  x coolify is reachable from anywhere past the host firewall: 0.0.0.0:8000->8080/tcp: DOCKER-USER
    has no filtering rules, and UFW's input rules do not apply to published ports
    DKR-001, critical, container:coolify/coolify
    rule: Published container ports do not bypass the host firewall
    fix:  Publish on 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1:5432:5432) or the tailnet address, or put the service
          behind the reverse proxy instead of publishing it. To keep a wildcard binding, filter it
          in DOCKER-USER (for example drop new connections on the public interface except from
          allowed sources), or install ufw-docker and open it with a route rule for the sources that
          need it.

  x SSH key folder is open to group or others (mode 0755, want 0700)
    SEC-003, critical, file:/data/coolify/ssh/keys
    rule: Platform SSH key folder is closed to other users
    fix:  chmod 700 the folder and chmod 600 every key in it.

  x UFW has IPV6=no while the host has a global IPv6 address: IPv6 traffic is not filtered
    NET-002, high
    rule: UFW filters IPv6 when the host has a global IPv6 address
    fix:  Set IPV6=yes in /etc/default/ufw, then ufw reload

  x coolify panel port 8000 listens on all interfaces and the firewall does not filter it
    PAAS-003, high, port:tcp/8000
    rule: Platform panel ports are not open to the world
    fix:  Reach the panel over the tailnet or behind an access proxy, and publish its ports on
          127.0.0.1 or the tailnet address.

  -- WARN (5) --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ! coolify-proxy mounts the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro); expected
    for a proxy, but it is root on the host if compromised; a read only mount does not stop
    connecting to a socket; managed by Coolify as its proxy: expected, a platform default the panel
    does not let you change
    DKR-010, critical, expected
    rule: No container mounts the Docker socket
    fix:  Remove the socket mount. If the container needs to read Docker state, put a socket proxy
          in front (for example tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy with only CONTAINERS=1) and point the
          container at it.

  ! tunnel-1 uses the host network (worst of 2 replicas)
    DKR-023, high, container:tunnel/cloudflared
    rule: No host network, PID or IPC namespace
    fix:  Use a bridge network and publish only the ports needed (on 127.0.0.1 behind the proxy);
          remove pid: host and ipc: host.

  ! running kernel 6.8.0-48-generic is older than installed 6.8.0-51-generic
    SYS-003, moderate
    rule: Running kernel is the newest installed
    fix:  Reboot to load the patched kernel.

  ! tcp/8000 is a published container port on wildcard and nothing filters it: DOCKER-USER has no
    filtering rules, and UFW's input rules do not apply to published ports (see DKR-001)
    NET-004, moderate
    rule: Exposure: every listening socket and who can reach it
    fix:  Bind services to 127.0.0.1 or the tailnet address instead of 0.0.0.0, or filter the port
          in the host firewall

  ! Docker Engine 27 left upstream support on 2025-05-03
    DKR-034, moderate
    rule: Docker Engine is supported upstream
    fix:  Upgrade Docker Engine from Docker's apt repository (docker-ce) to a supported release
          line.
